findings.text: — §2 introduces `crew dispatch --model` and a "backends each listing its models" shape without citing the model machinery that already resolves a per-backend `model` into launch argv, nor the schema's existing scalar `model` and `catalog` fields (reckon/_backends.py:1183,1526 expand `backend["model"]` into `-m`/`--model`; reckon/_flight_schema.py:293 declares `model`, and `catalog` — which already matches a configured model against a backend's served list). The plan therefore does not say whether `--model` selects among a backend's declared members or reuses the existing field, and a reader cannot tell which resolution path it extends.

— §6 says the graded open/pace/hold state is "pushed to every follower as one line", but names no emission point and never says why the follower's existing watch/transition stream — the ticker rows and per-run `to_state` transitions the follower already renders (reckon/crew/ticker.py; reckon/cli.py follower; reckon/crew/query.py:891 `state_changes`) — cannot carry it. A new push with no stated seam risks a second delivery path beside the one the follower already reads.

— §4 introduces an explicit `review_fallback` list ("clive then codex on this host") beside the mechanism that already owns review-lane ordering: `_ordered_review_lanes` (reckon/crew/recovery.py:2075) orders candidates as owning lane, then local, then a stable alphabetical tail, and `review_excluded_backends` (reckon/schema/flight.yaml:225, read via `recovery._review_excluded_backends`, recovery.py:2038) is the declared control that removes metered lanes. §4's "Done when `_review_lane_candidates` reads an ordered fallback list and has no alphabetical tail" is a change to the owner, but the plan never names it — it proposes a second key governing the same ordering.

— against this week's figures (public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23), §3 adds a `--permission "<lead's words>" gate on the claude backend, which is both a new cli_option and a new refusal family ("a claude dispatch without a permission reason refuses"), and states neither what it retires or merges nor why nothing can be. The plan's §2 already retires per-model backend entries under the merge clause, so the vocabulary to account for added surface exists and §3 does not use it.

— §7 adds `crew follow --until-actionable`, a new cli_option (contributing to the cli_options 317 figure), without naming what it retires or merges or why nothing can be; the existing `crew follow` command already carries `--session`, `--observe-session`, `--run` and a deprecated `--attention` (reckon/cli.py:4693), so a merge candidate exists and is unaddressed.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §5's `paid_lanes.py` composes three recorded sources into one document behind a resolver and a single renderer, hiding source reconciliation, per-window recency and the staleness rule; the other sections extend existing modules (`dispatch.py`, `recovery.py`, `lane_document.py`) rather than adding shallow new ones.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4's `review_fallback` is a second ordering key beside the existing ordered review-lane mechanism and its exclusion control.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §3 adds a CLI option and a refusal family without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be, and §7 adds a CLI option on the same terms.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 proposes `--model` and per-backend "member models" without citing the existing per-backend `model` expansion or the schema's `model`/`catalog` fields; §4 likewise omits the existing ordered review-lane mechanism it would sit beside.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §6 adds a graded lane-state line pushed to every follower without naming the existing follower transition stream it should extend.
